character_sheet: A passive whale: a 20x12x52 body with a belly slab and a back ridge, a 16x8x22 head with a hinged lower jaw plate, a small dorsal fin, two flippers of a root and a 22-long blade, and a tail of two pieces ending in a pair of flukes (ModelWhale.java:56-124, fourteen parts). 100 HP, speed 0.35, no attack (Whale.java:69-74). It drifts with the current (pushed by fluid, :120-123), is tempted by cod (:62), panics when hurt (:63), breeds on a crystal apple (:61, :239-242) and, stranded, scans up to ten blocks for water and heads there at 1.0, drying out 4 HP at a time when none is found (:134-159); in water it splashes and heals (:161-165). Every 250-500 ticks it blows: a 25-50-tick spout of bubble and splash particles above its back (:46-47, :80-113). It spawns in daylight above y 50 on a 1-in-50 roll with no other whale within 32 (:203-211; ModEntities.java:414-415). Read it as a whale: a slow flipper beat, the tail flukes pumping up and down with a lag along the chain, the jaw barely breathing.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig, x0.5 as a baby (WhaleRenderer.java:31, :43-47; shadow 0.1, :29) on a 256x256 sheet (ModelWhale.java:126), whale.png (WhaleRenderer.java:21); the hitbox is 1.5 x 2.5 (ModEntities.java:414-415). The tail is a position chain: the code places the second piece 14 px along the first and the flukes 8 px along the second each tick (ModelWhale.java:152-156) - key the joints, not the positions.

labels.belly: belly slab (12x2x32 under the body; static)
labels.back: back ridge (8x2x40 along the top; static)
labels.backfin: dorsal fin (1x4x8 raked back 21 deg; static)
labels.head: head (16x8x22 ahead of the body; static — no look)
labels.jaw: lower jaw plate (14x2x20 hinged under the head; breathes 3.6 deg about 0.087 rad)
labels.lfin1: left flipper, root (4x3x6; rolls at half the blade's angle)
labels.lfin2: left flipper, blade (22x2x8; rolls with the fin group about 0.436 rad)
labels.rfin2: right flipper, blade (the mirror, about -0.436 rad)
labels.tail1: tail, first piece (12x7x14; pitches at half the tail wave)
labels.tail2: tail, second piece (8x5x10, placed 14 along the first; pitches at 1.25x the wave)

labels.tailfin2: left fluke (the mirror; pitches with the right fluke)

groups.name: gait
groups.axis: z (the flippers) and x (the tail chain, with its y / z positions)
groups.amplitude: flippers, moving (limbSwingAmount > 0.1): pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) x the walking speed about ±0.436 rad at 0.3 rad/tick, the root at half the blade's angle; still: pi x 0.05 = 0.157 rad (9 deg) at 0.08 rad/tick, unscaled. Tail, moving: pi x 0.16 = 0.503 rad (29 deg) x the speed at 0.4 rad/tick - the first piece at 0.5x (14 deg), the second at 1.25x (36 deg), the flukes at 2.25x (65 deg); still: pi x 0.03 = 0.094 rad (5 deg) at 0.05 rad/tick, the same ratios; the second piece is placed 14 px along the first's pitch and the flukes 8 px along the second's
groups.plain: the two flippers beat up and down together, the roots at half the blades' angle, while the tail pumps with the swing growing from the root to the flukes: broad strokes on the move, a slow waft and a gentle pump at rest
groups.math: f = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 0.3) * pi * 0.2 * amount : cos(t * 0.08) * pi * 0.05; lfin2.zRot = 0.436 + f; lfin1.zRot = lfin2.zRot / 2; rfin2.zRot = -0.436 - f; rfin1.zRot = rfin2.zRot / 2; a = amount > 0.1 ? cos(t * 0.4) * pi * 0.16 * amount : cos(t * 0.05) * pi * 0.03; tail1.xRot = a * 0.5; tail2.xRot = a * 1.25; tailfin1.xRot = tailfin2.xRot = a * 2.25; tail2.z = tail1.z + cos(tail1.xRot) * 14; tail2.y = tail1.y - sin(tail1.xRot) * 14; tailfin.z = tail2.z + cos(tail2.xRot) * 8; tailfin.y = tail2.y - sin(tail2.xRot) * 8
groups.phase: the limbSwingAmount threshold of 0.1 selects each rhythm (one gait group per rig: the generator's rule, so the flippers and the tail share this group)
groups.omega_note: the classic phases are ageInTicks x 0.3 for the flippers (a 20.9-tick period; x 0.08 at rest, 78.5 ticks) and x 0.4 for the tail (15.7 ticks; x 0.05 at rest, 126 ticks)

groups.name: jaw
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.02 = 0.063 rad (3.6 deg) about a 0.087 rad rest
groups.plain: the jaw plate breathes very slowly open and shut at all times
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.03: the natural period is 209 ticks (10.5 s)

behaviour: Two gait-scaled rhythms with a rest branch at a limbSwingAmount of 0.1 (ModelWhale.java:132-156): on the move the flippers beat 36 degrees x the walking speed at 0.3 rad/tick and the tail pumps 29 degrees x the speed at 0.4 rad/tick, the swing multiplied 0.5 / 1.25 / 2.25 from the first piece to the flukes; at rest the same shapes run slow and small - a 9-degree waft at 0.08 and a 5-degree pump at 0.05 - so a still whale never freezes.

The jaw plate breathes 3.6 degrees about its 5-degree rest at 0.03 rad/tick, a 10-second cycle (:141-142). The body, belly, back ridge, dorsal fin and head are static; the head does not follow the look.

The same formulas draw it in water and on land: setupAnim has no water branch, so the swim and the stranded crawl toward water (Whale.java:134-159) differ only in speed. The spout (:80-113) is particles on a timer, not a pose.

wishlist: in `swim`: the code's tail is a straight up-and-down pump (ModelWhale.java:148-150) — give the flukes a lag behind the second piece and a roll of the body into the stroke
in `idle`: the slow waft the code has (:134, :146) plus a rise and fall of the whole body, as a whale hangs at the surface
in `spout`: an arch of the back and a lift of the flukes timed to the 25-50-tick particle spout (Whale.java:84-87)
in `walk` (the stranded crawl, Whale.java:134-159): a heave with the flippers rather than the swim beat
formulas: `ModelWhale.setupAnim` (ModelWhale.java:130-157; orig ModelWhale.java:120-135 in `render` (func_78088_a, :117-150; func_78087_a at :158-160 is a bare super call); no wingspeed - `new ModelWhale()` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:484): the fin angle is the cosine of the age in ticks times 0.3, times pi, times 0.2, times the walking speed while the walking speed is above a tenth, else the cosine of the age times 0.08, times pi, times 0.05; the left outer fin rolls by 0.436 plus it and the left inner fin by half of that, the right outer fin by -0.436 minus it and the right inner fin by half of that. The jaw pitches by 0.087 plus the cosine of the age times 0.03, times pi, times 0.02. The tail angle is the cosine of the age times 0.4, times pi, times 0.16, times the walking speed above the threshold, else the cosine of the age times 0.05, times pi, times 0.03; the first tail link pitches by half of it, the second by 1.25 of it and both flukes by 2.25 of it; the second link is placed 14 units along the cosine of the first link's pitch in z and 14 units back along its sine in y from the first link's bind pivot, and the two flukes 8 units along the second link's pitch the same way from the second link. The head angles and the entity's state play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (WhaleGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
